rationale: Evidence from iteration 2 (score 563.9, best so far): the oval is solved (20/20 finished, max_error 0.035). The s-bend finishes 11/20 and fails 9/20 by off_track. The slalom fails 20/20 by off_track at progress 0.17, with max_error about 0.065 and about 1 line-loss event per run. Steering oscillation is low (0.19 to 0.39), so the robot is not jittering. It is reacting too slowly to fast alternating bends and drifting past the 0.06 m off-track limit. The limit is fixed at 0.06 m for this body width, because a 0.12 to 0.18 m body does not raise it above 0.06 m. Changes: (1) Raise kp from 2.0 to 2.6 for a stronger correction per unit of sensor offset. The signal scale is unchanged, so the increase is a pure gain change. (2) Raise kd from 0.6 to 0.9 to damp the larger correction, since oscillation has margin (about 0.3 against an observed ceiling in the oval). (3) Narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which raises yaw rate per unit of wheel differential and gives the steering more authority on tight bends. Mass, sensor array (seven sensors, x = -0.06 to +0.06, y = 0.05), sensor weights, base_speed (1.0) and line_loss (last_direction) are kept, so the change is mostly about steering agility. Expected result: slalom progress rises above 0.5 with fewer off-track ends, and s-bend finish rate rises above 0.55. The oval should remain near 950. Hypotheses to test next: (a) if max_error on the slalom stays near 0.06 while oscillation stays low, steering is still too slow, so raise kp further (toward 3.0) and consider a sensor array further forward; (b) if oscillation rises above about 0.5 on the oval, kd is too low relative to kp; (c) if the robot finishes reliably but completion_time is above 2.5 s, raise base_speed toward 1.2 to 1.3.
